Hi Olivia — great to hear from you and glad the demo was helpful. Attaching the hosted API rate card (Novapay_RateCard_v2.pdf) and a short tokenization note below. High-level answers up front:

- We bill per-token and by default use the tokenizer that matches the model variant you call (so the same raw text can yield different billed tokens depending on model).
- For English your token delta is typically small (1–5% between modern SentencePiece and GPT-style BPE). For mixed-language (English+Spanish) you may see slightly larger deltas (~5–15%) depending on text morphology and sentence segmentation.

Tokenization samples (short):
- English sample: "Today I transferred $2,500 to the client."
  - GPT2-BPE (gpt-3.5-like): ~9 tokens
  - mT5 SentencePiece (multilingual): ~10 tokens

- Spanish sample: "Transferí 2.500 USD al cliente hoy."
  - GPT2-BPE: ~8 tokens
  - mT5 SentencePiece: ~10 tokens

Notes and implications:
- Billing: because tokenization differs by model, a switch in model family will change your billed tokens even if the input is the same. We provide a small tool (link below) so you can run representative inputs against both tokenizers to quantify the delta before committing.
- Packaging: for pilots we recommend starting on the hosted API with a month-to-month usage commitment; if you expect steady usage (>=10M tokens/month) we can discuss committed discounts or a reserved capacity plan that smooths tokenization variance into predictable unit pricing.

Next steps: Rafael (cc'd) can run a 500-sentence sample through both tokenizers and return exact deltas; Marissa can propose a pilot discount schedule. Would 30 minutes on Friday work for a joint call?

Attaching: Novapay_RateCard_v2.pdf (our hosted API list prices + standard pilot discounts).

Best,
Laura Bennett

Hi Olivia — quick technical follow-up from our infra side. A few important clarifications:

1) We compute billed tokens using the tokenizer implementation that matches the model you invoke. That means if you call a gpt-3.5-style endpoint, we run the GPT-BPE tokenizer server-side for billing and execution. If you call a multilingual mT5 variant, we use its SentencePiece implementation.

2) Token-count variance depends on language and punctuation. For a few representative samples I ran locally (attached tokenization-sample.csv):
   - EN paragraph (approx. 85 words): GPT-BPE = 42 tokens, SentencePiece (mT5) = 48 tokens (~14% increase)
   - ES paragraph (approx. 78 words): GPT-BPE = 39 tokens, SentencePiece = 47 tokens (~21% increase)

3) Rounding/discounting: billing is exact per the model tokenizer; we do not normalize token counts across models by default. However, for committed customers we can offer a contractual unit-price that abstracts away tokenizer variance (e.g., agree on a per-1k token price that applies regardless of model). That is typically handled in a reserved capacity / contract amendment.

4) Implementation note: if you want predictable billing while experimenting with multiple model families, two options: a) pick a canonical model family for production and use it for billing-sensitive calls; b) sign a committed usage agreement and we set contract-level unit pricing.

I attached the CSV with the example sentences and exact token counts so you can inspect. Happy to run your real payloads if you share a small sample.

-Rafael Mendes
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
